at ødelægge.explanation: "At ødelægge" means "to destroy" or "to break" something so it no longer works: Jeg ødelagde min telefon (I broke my phone). If a thing just stops working by itself, say Den gik i stykker (It broke).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **ødelægge** den gamle vase.
sentence.en: The children must not break the old vase.

at øge.explanation: "At øge" means "to increase", making something bigger or more: Vi øger farten (We increase the speed). When something goes up by itself, use at stige (to rise): Prisen stiger (The price is rising).

sentence.en: The company will increase the price next year.

at ønske.explanation: "At ønske" means "to wish", often to wish someone something: Jeg ønsker dig en god tur (I wish you a good trip). Hvad ønsker De? (What would you like?) is a polite question in a shop.

sentence.da: Vi vil **ønske** hende tillykke i morgen.
sentence.en: We want to wish her congratulations tomorrow.

at ønske sig.explanation: "At ønske sig" means "to wish for" something you would like to get, such as a gift: Jeg ønsker mig en cykel (I wish for a bike). Without sig, at ønske (to wish) is more general: Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke (I wish you good luck).

sentence.da: Børn plejer at **ønske sig** en hund til jul.
sentence.en: Kids usually wish for a dog for Christmas.

at øve.explanation: "At øve" means "to practice". Danish usually adds mig (myself): Jeg øver mig i dansk means "I am practicing Danish". The thing you practice comes after i (in).

sentence.da: Hun skal **øve** sig i at spille klaver.
sentence.en: She has to practice playing the piano.

at øve sig.explanation: "At øve sig" means "to practice" to get better: Jeg øver mig hver dag (I practice every day). The little word changes with who practices: mig (myself), dig (yourself), sig (himself / herself).

sentence.da: Han skal **øve sig** i dansk hver dag.
sentence.en: He has to practice Danish every day.

en ø.explanation: "En ø" means "an island", land with water all around it.

sentence.da: Vi tager færgen til en lille **ø**.
sentence.en: We take the ferry to a small island.

en øjenfarve.explanation: "En øjenfarve" means "an eye color", built from øje (eye) and farve (color). Ask Hvad er din øjenfarve? (What is your eye color?) and answer Jeg har brune øjne (I have brown eyes).

sentence.da: Min **øjenfarve** er grøn, og min fars er blå.
sentence.en: My eye color is green, and my father's is blue.

en økonomi.explanation: "En økonomi" means "an economy", how a country or a household handles its finances: Min økonomi er dårlig (My finances are bad).

sentence.en: The country's economy is strong.

en økse.explanation: "En økse" means "an axe", the tool for chopping wood. The matching verb is at hugge (to chop): Jeg hugger brænde (I chop firewood).

sentence.da: Vi hugger træ med en skarp **økse**.
sentence.en: We chop wood with a sharp axe.

en øl.explanation: "En øl" means "a beer". The plural is also "øl": to øl means "two beers". You can say en stor øl (a large beer) or en lille øl (a small beer).

sentence.en: I drink a cold beer.

en ølflaske.explanation: "En ølflaske" means "a beer bottle". It is built from øl (beer) and flaske (bottle). Most carry pant (a refundable deposit) that you get back when you return the bottle.

sentence.da: Øl er i en **ølflaske**, og vin er i en vinflaske.
sentence.en: Beer is in a beer bottle, and wine is in a wine bottle.

en ønskeseddel.explanation: "En ønskeseddel" means "a wish list", a list of presents you hope to get. It is built from ønske (wish) and seddel (note), which also means a banknote: en hundredkroneseddel (a hundred-krone banknote).

sentence.da: Hun skrev en lang **ønskeseddel** til jul.
sentence.en: She wrote a long wish list for Christmas.

en ørering.explanation: "En ørering" means "an earring". For two, say et par øreringe (a pair of earrings).

sentence.en: I have lost my left earring.

en ørken.explanation: "En ørken" means "a desert", a dry, sandy land. Do not mix it up with en dessert (a dessert) after dinner.

sentence.da: Der er næsten ingen regn i en **ørken**.
sentence.en: There is almost no rain in a desert.

en ørn.explanation: "En ørn" means "an eagle", a large bird that hunts other animals and flies very high.

sentence.en: An eagle flies high over the mountains.

en øse.explanation: "En øse" means "a ladle", a deep scoop with a long handle for serving food from a pot. The action is at øse op (to scoop out): Han øser maden op (He scoops out the food). Op adds the idea of lifting out of the pot.

sentence.da: Han tager suppe op af gryden med en **øse**.
sentence.en: He takes soup out of the pot with a ladle.

en øvelse.explanation: "En øvelse" means "an exercise", a task for practicing: Vi laver en øvelse i timen (We do an exercise in class). It also means a workout move: Den øvelse er svær (That exercise is hard).

sentence.da: Børnene laver en **øvelse** i matematik hver dag.
sentence.en: The children do a math exercise every day.

et øje.explanation: "Et øje" means "an eye", the part of the body you see with.

sentence.en: I have something in my eye.

et øjeblik.explanation: "Et øjeblik" means "a moment", a very short time. The word is made of øje (eye) and blik (glance). Danes also say i øjeblikket (right now): Jeg læser i øjeblikket (I am reading right now).

sentence.en: Wait a moment, please.

et øjenbryn.explanation: "Et øjenbryn" means "an eyebrow", the line of hair above your eye. As in English, it is used for surprise: Han løftede et øjenbryn (He raised an eyebrow).

sentence.da: Han har et ar over det venstre **øjenbryn**.
sentence.en: He has a scar over his left eyebrow.

et ønske.explanation: "Et ønske" means "a wish", something you want to happen. The same word is also the verb at ønske (to wish): Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke (I wish you good luck).

sentence.en: Her biggest wish is a dog.

et øre.explanation: "Et øre" means "an ear", the part of the body you hear with. The same word is also a tiny coin worth a hundredth of a krone.

sentence.en: My ear hurts.

ødelagt.explanation: "Ødelagt" means "broken" or "ruined", for something that no longer works at all or cannot be saved. It also fits a day or a plan: Dagen er ødelagt (The day is ruined).

sentence.da: Min telefon er **ødelagt**, fordi jeg tabte den.
sentence.en: My phone is broken because I dropped it.

økologisk.explanation: "Økologisk" means "organic", mostly for food and farms. In shops it is often shortened to øko on labels: øko-æg (organic eggs).

sentence.en: I prefer to buy organic milk.

økonomisk.explanation: "Økonomisk" means "economic" and "financial", about money. It can also mean "cheap to run": en økonomisk bil (an economical car).

sentence.en: We need financial help.

øm.explanation: "Øm" means "sore" or "tender", when a part of the body hurts a little, especially when touched. It is milder than ondt (pain), as in Jeg har ondt i armen (My arm hurts).

sentence.en: My shoulder is sore after exercise.

øreringe.explanation: "Øreringe" means "earrings", jewelry you wear in your ears.

sentence.en: She has small earrings in her ears.

øst.explanation: "Øst" means "east". It is also part of place names such as Østjylland (eastern Jutland).

sentence.en: The sun rises in the east.

østersøen.explanation: "Østersøen" means "the Baltic Sea", the sea east of Denmark. The name has øst (east) in it because of where the sea lies.

sentence.en: The ferry sails across the Baltic Sea to Poland.

østpå.explanation: "Østpå" means "eastward", toward the east, for movement. For a place, use øst for (east of): København ligger øst for Roskilde (Copenhagen is east of Roskilde).

sentence.en: We are heading east after lunch.
